what: Which body a crowded cell answers with is now named on the command line, not only decided by WorldLabels.BodiesAt's fixed order. -SelectBodyIndex (--select-body-index engine-side) picks the zero-based position in that order; two frames of the same crowded cell with two different indices are the proof, per the Issue's own wording.

base.howObtained: git worktree add ../_wt-373-focus-flag -b feature/373-focus-flag origin/main, then git rev-parse HEAD

scene.why: The cell Issue #373 names as holding six bodies: one crew member (Тишина) and five raiders sharing one tile.

index0.controlFeedback: (15,7): 1 of 6 standing here; click the cell again for the next one.
index0.inspector: CREATURE #8 · Тишина — ALIVE HP 1/28 (a crew member: WorldLabels.BodiesAt lists crew first, by id, so index 0 is her)

index3.controlFeedback: (15,7): 4 of 6 standing here; click the cell again for the next one.
index3.inspector: CELL (15, 7) — generic cell panel, not a creature panel: index 3 (the fourth of six) is a raider.

reading.sameCanonicalState: Both runs print the identical checksum (f8e26b05...) — selecting a different body never touches PrototypeWorld, same invariant as every selection path before this Issue.
reading.differentFrame: The two PNGs have different sha256 (085e2d0a... vs 8bf7806b...) and different feedback ("1 of 6" vs "4 of 6"), and the inspector panel switches between a named creature card and the generic cell card depending on which population the chosen index lands in. That is the named, reproducible, managed choice Issue #373 asks for: two frames, two bodies, both provable from the printed state rather than from eyeballing a crowd of overlapping sprites.
reading.outOfRangeGuard: An index the cell does not have throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException("--select-body-index", ...) naming the cell and how many bodies it actually holds, the same refuse-rather-than-clamp style --select-creature already uses for an unknown id.
